raw_response:
I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I’m not going to change too much just because someone says there is a new way. Cotton is what I know, and on 12 mu I can still manage it carefully. I have well water, so I’m not as exposed as the dryland people, but pumping costs money, and with only two people in the house I also have to think about labor. At my age, I don’t want to chase a very high yield with very heavy input. I’d rather keep the stand uniform, feed the crop in splits, irrigate at the key stages, and spend money where it protects yield. I’ll plant in the usual mid-April window if soil moisture is right. For seed, I’ll use a locally available improved cotton variety with good boll setting and decent disease tolerance, not the cheapest saved seed. For fertilizer, I’ll put most of the phosphorus and potassium in before planting, then split nitrogen so I don’t waste it early. If the crop looks weak after first square, I can add a little more, but I won’t push too hard. Irrigation I’ll probably do twice, maybe three times if summer turns dry, because cotton can stand some stress but not too much at flowering and boll set. Pesticide I won’t spray by calendar only; I’ll watch aphids, bollworm, and weeds, then act when I see pressure. Harvest I expect to do mostly by family labor with some hired help if picking comes together too fast.
